lessons.title: Say hello
lessons.canDo: Start and end a friendly conversation
lessons.scenario: Smarty wakes up in his bedroom and greets his friend Mia.

items.note: Say 'Hello' to greet anyone in a friendly way.
Say 'Hi' for a quick, casual hello with friends.
Say 'Goodbye' when you leave someone.
Say 'Bye' for a short, friendly goodbye.

practice.prompt: You meet Smarty in his bedroom. Which word starts the conversation?
practice.explanation: Hello is a friendly greeting to start a conversation.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Hi is a short, friendly way to say hello.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with a similar meaning.
practice.explanation: Hello and Hi both greet someone; Goodbye and Bye both end a chat.

practice.prompt: Mia leaves Smarty's bedroom. Complete what she says.
practice.explanation: Say Goodbye when you leave someone.

practice.prompt: Build a short goodbye to Leo.
practice.explanation: Bye is a short, friendly way to say goodbye.

practice.prompt: Say the greeting and request aloud.
practice.explanation: Start with Hello to greet someone politely.

story.hook: Who visits Smarty in his bedroom?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat waves hello from his cozy bedroom doorway as Mia the tabby cat walks in and waves back.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: S - M - A - R - T - Y.

questions.explanation: Mia says: Hi, Smarty!

questions.prompt: What does Smarty say when Mia leaves?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: Goodbye, Mia!

mission.setup: You visit Smarty in his bedroom. Say hello and then say goodbye.

turns.hint: Say Hello or Hi to Smarty.
Say Goodbye or Bye.

lessons.title: My name is
lessons.canDo: Introduce yourself and ask a name
lessons.scenario: Smarty meets a new cat named Ben in his bedroom.

items.note: Say 'My name is…' followed by your name to introduce yourself.
Say 'I am…' with your name as another simple way to introduce yourself.
Ask 'What is your name?' when you meet someone new.
Ask 'And you?' to bounce the same question back to the other person.

grammar.title: Introducing yourself with be
grammar.explanation: Use 'am' after 'I' (I am Sam) and 'is' after 'my name' or 'what' (My name is Sam. What is your name?).

practice.prompt: Smarty wants to know who you are. What does he ask?
practice.explanation: Ask 'What is your name?' to learn someone's name.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: My name is Ben introduces the speaker's name.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself as Zara. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use I with am: I am Zara.

practice.prompt: Build the question to ask someone's name.
practice.explanation: Put What is first, followed by your name.

practice.prompt: Match the sentences that go together.
practice.explanation: My name is Leo and I am Leo both introduce Leo.

practice.prompt: You told Sam your name. Ask for his name back.
practice.explanation: Say 'And you?' to ask the other person the same question.

practice.prompt: Say the introduction aloud.
practice.text: Hello! My name is Tom. And you?
practice.answer: Hello! My name is Tom. And you?
practice.explanation: Greet, state your name with My name is, and ask And you?

story.hook: How does Ben spell his name for Smarty?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Smarty the black cat shakes paws with Ben, an orange cat wearing a blue scarf.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hello! I am Smarty. What is your name?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Hi, Smarty! My name is Ben.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: S - M - A - R - T - Y!

questions.prompt: What is the orange cat's name?
questions.explanation: Ben says: My name is Ben.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty ask Ben first?
questions.explanation: Smarty asks: What is your name?

mission.setup: Smarty wants to know your name. Introduce yourself!

turns.hint: Say 'My name is…' or 'I am…' with a name like Zara or Leo.

turns.smarty: I am Smarty. How do you spell your name?
accept: ^(?:m i a|s a m|b e n|l e o|a n a|l i l y|o m a r|z a r a|t o m)$
turns.hint: Spell the name letter by letter, like Z A R A.

lessons.title: Thank you
lessons.scenario: Leo drops pencils in Smarty's bedroom and Smarty helps him.

items.note: Say 'Sorry' when you make a mistake or bump into someone.
Add 'please' when you ask someone to do something.
Say 'Thank you' when someone helps you or gives you something.
Say 'Thanks' for a quick, friendly thank-you.

practice.prompt: You bump into Sam by mistake. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Say Sorry when you make a small mistake.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Thank you shows gratitude when someone helps you.

practice.prompt: Ask Zara politely to say her name again.
practice.explanation: Use please to make a request polite.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases with a similar meaning.
practice.explanation: Thanks is a shorter way to say Thank you.

practice.prompt: Build a short thank-you to Leo.
practice.explanation: Say Thanks followed by the person's name.

practice.prompt: Say the apology and thank-you aloud.
practice.explanation: Use Sorry to apologize and Thank you to show appreciation.

story.hook: Why does Leo say sorry to Smarty?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Leo the gray cat accidentally drops three colorful pencils on the rug while Smarty helps pick them up.

questions.prompt: What does Leo say after Smarty helps him?
questions.explanation: Leo says: Thank you, Smarty! Thanks!

questions.prompt: Which polite word does Smarty use when he asks Leo to repeat?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: Repeat that, please.

mission.setup: Smarty helps you in his bedroom. Be polite!

turns.hint: Tell Smarty your name using 'I am…' or 'My name is…'.
Say Thank you or Thanks.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty reviews greetings, introductions, and polite words with Mia and Sam.

practice.prompt: You meet Sam for the first time. Ask his name.
practice.explanation: Use 'What is your name?' to ask someone's name.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: My name is Mia. And you?
practice.answer: My name is Mia. And you?
options: My name is Mia. And you?
practice.explanation: Mia states her name and asks 'And you?' in return.

practice.prompt: Match the pairs with similar meaning.
practice.explanation: Each pair matches a full phrase with its shorter friendly form.

practice.prompt: Apologize to Smarty. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Say Sorry when you make a mistake.

practice.prompt: Build the polite request.
practice.explanation: End the request with please to sound polite.

practice.prompt: Introduce yourself and say thank you aloud.
practice.explanation: Combine I am with your name and Thank you.

story.hook: Do Mia and Sam remember their polite words?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat stands by his bedroom bookshelf as Mia and Sam introduce themselves politely.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello! I am Mia. What is your name?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Hi, Mia! My name is Sam.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: S - A - M. Thank you! And you?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: M - I - A. Thanks, Sam! Goodbye!

questions.explanation: Sam says: My name is Sam.

questions.prompt: What does Mia say before she leaves?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Thanks, Sam! Goodbye!

mission.setup: Have a short conversation with Smarty using what you learned in lessons 1 to 3.

turns.smarty: Hi! I am Smarty. What is your name?
turns.hint: Say Hi and tell Smarty your name.
Thank Smarty and say Goodbye or Bye.

lessons.title: You are, he is
lessons.canDo: Use the right form of be
lessons.scenario: Smarty points out his friends in a photo in his bedroom.

items.note: Use 'You are' when talking directly to someone.
Use 'He is' when talking about one boy or man.
Use 'She is' when talking about one girl or woman.
Use 'We are' for yourself and at least one other person together.

grammar.title: Forms of be: am, is, are
grammar.explanation: Match 'be' to the person: I am, you are, he is, she is, and we are.

practice.prompt: Talk about Ana, a girl. Which phrase fits?
practice.explanation: Use She is for one girl or woman.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: He is is used for one boy or man.

practice.prompt: Speak directly to Sam. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use are after you: You are Sam.

practice.prompt: Talk about Tom, a boy. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use He for a boy or man: He is Tom.

practice.prompt: Talk about Lily and Mia together. Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use We are for two or more people including yourself.

practice.prompt: Match each pronoun with the right form of be.
practice.explanation: I goes with am, he goes with is, and we goes with are.

practice.prompt: Say both sentences aloud.
practice.text: She is Zara. He is Ben.
practice.answer: She is Zara. He is Ben.
practice.explanation: Use She is for Zara and He is for Ben.

story.hook: Who is in the picture with Smarty and Mia?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Smarty and Mia look at a framed group photo showing Leo and Ana smiling.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! You are Smarty, and I am Mia.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We are one, two, three, four!

questions.prompt: How does Mia talk about Leo?
questions.explanation: Mia says: He is Leo.

questions.prompt: How does Smarty talk about Ana?
questions.explanation: Smarty says: And she is Ana!

mission.setup: Smarty asks about you, Mia, and Leo. Use the right form of 'be'.

turns.hint: Say 'I am…' with your name, or 'You are Smarty'.

accept: ^(?:she is|she s) mia(?: and (?:he is|he s) leo)?$
turns.example: She is Mia and he is Leo.
turns.hint: Say 'She is Mia' or 'He is Leo'.

lessons.title: Time of day
lessons.scenario: Smarty greets friends in his bedroom in the morning, afternoon, and evening.

items.note: Say 'Good morning' when you greet someone before lunch.
Say 'Good afternoon' from around noon until early evening.
Say 'Good evening' when you greet someone later in the day.
Say 'See you later' when you say goodbye and plan to meet again.

practice.prompt: You wake up and see Smarty. Which greeting fits?
practice.explanation: Use Good morning in the early part of the day.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Good afternoon is used after noon.

practice.prompt: It is 7 PM and you meet Ben. Complete the greeting.
practice.explanation: Say Good evening when greeting someone at night or late in the day.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases that go together.
practice.explanation: See you later is a friendly way to say Goodbye.

practice.prompt: Build the goodbye phrase.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: See you later!

practice.prompt: Say the morning greeting and introduce yourself aloud.
practice.explanation: Start with Good morning and introduce yourself with I am.

story.hook: Who visits Smarty in the evening?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom with stars outside the window, Smarty greets Omar in the evening before saying see you later.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: She is Mia, and he is Sam.

questions.explanation: Smarty says: Good evening, Omar!

questions.prompt: What do Smarty and Omar say at the end?
questions.explanation: Both Smarty and Omar say: See you later!

mission.setup: Greet Smarty for the time of day, then say goodbye.

turns.hint: Say Good morning, Good afternoon, or Good evening.
Say 'See you later'.

lessons.title: Where are you from?
lessons.canDo: Say where you are from and ask someone else
lessons.scenario: Smarty looks at a world globe in his bedroom with Zara and Leo.

items.note: Say 'I am from…' followed by your country or city.
Ask 'Where are you from?' to learn someone's home country or city.
Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia; start country names with a capital letter.
Brazil is a large country in South America; always capitalize country names.
England is part of the United Kingdom; start it with a capital letter.

grammar.title: Where questions with be
grammar.explanation: Put 'Where' first, then 'am / is / are', then the person: Where are you from? Where is she from?

practice.prompt: Ask a new friend about their home country.
practice.explanation: Use Where are you from? to ask about someone's home country.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Listen for the country name Uzbekistan at the end.

practice.prompt: Ana is from South America. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Brazil is the country in South America.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about Tom.
practice.explanation: Use from before a country name: He is from England.

practice.prompt: Build the question.
practice.explanation: Start with Where, then are you from?

practice.prompt: Match each question with its answer.
practice.explanation: Match you with I, he with He, and she with She.

practice.prompt: Say where you are from and ask back aloud.
practice.text: I am from Uzbekistan. And you?
practice.answer: I am from Uzbekistan. And you?
practice.explanation: Use I am from plus the country, then ask And you?

story.hook: Where are Zara and Leo from?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Smarty spins a colorful globe on his desk while chatting with Zara and Leo.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good afternoon, Zara! Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: I am from Uzbekistan. And you, Leo?

questions.explanation: Zara says: I am from Uzbekistan.
Leo says: I am from Brazil!

mission.setup: Tell Smarty where you are from and ask him where he is from.

turns.hint: Say 'I am from' and Uzbekistan, Brazil, or England.
Ask 'Where are you from?' or guess 'You are from England'.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.scenario: Smarty reviews forms of be, time greetings, and countries with Ana and Tom.

practice.prompt: You meet Ana at 9 AM. Which greeting fits?
practice.explanation: Use Good morning before noon.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: We are is used when talking about yourself and others together.

practice.prompt: Ask someone about their home country.
practice.explanation: Use Where to ask about a place or country.

practice.prompt: Match each sentence with the person or people it describes.
practice.explanation: He is for Tom, She is for Zara, and We are for Mia and Sam.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Ana.
practice.explanation: Use She is before from Brazil.

practice.prompt: Say the afternoon greeting and goodbye aloud.
practice.explanation: Greet with Good afternoon and say See you later when leaving.

story.hook: Are Ana and Tom from the same country?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Smarty introduces Ana and Tom next to a colorful world map on the wall.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good afternoon! She is Ana, and he is Tom.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Hello, Tom! I am from Brazil. Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Hi, Ana! I am from England.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: We are Smarty, Ana, and Tom!

questions.explanation: Tom says: I am from England.
Smarty says: Good afternoon!

mission.setup: Greet Smarty and say where you are from.

turns.smarty: Good evening! Where are you from?
turns.example: Good evening! I am from Uzbekistan.
turns.hint: Greet Smarty and say 'I am from…'.
Say 'See you later'.

lessons.title: How are you?
lessons.scenario: Smarty checks in on Mia and Ben in his bedroom after a long day.

items.note: Ask 'How are you?' to check how someone is feeling.
Say 'I am fine' when you are doing well.
Say 'I am happy' when you feel joyful and good.
Say 'I am tired' when you feel sleepy or need rest.

practice.prompt: You want to ask Smarty how he feels. What do you say?
practice.explanation: Ask 'How are you?' to ask about someone's feelings.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: I am fine, thank you! is a polite way to say you feel well.

practice.prompt: Ben feels sleepy in the evening. Complete what he says.
practice.explanation: Say I am tired when you need sleep or rest.

practice.prompt: Match each question or statement with the best match.
practice.explanation: How are you? is answered with I am fine, thanks!

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.explanation: Put I am before happy.

practice.prompt: Answer politely and ask back aloud.
practice.text: I am fine, thank you! And you?
practice.answer: I am fine, thank you! And you?
practice.explanation: Say I am fine, thank you! and return the question with And you?

story.hook: How does Ben feel in Smarty's bedroom?

image.describe: In Smarty's cozy bedroom, Mia smiles happily while Ben yawns sleepily on a soft beanbag chair.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good evening, Mia! How are you?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I am fine, thank you! I am happy! And you?

questions.explanation: Ben says: I am tired!
Mia says: I am happy!

mission.setup: Smarty asks how you are. Answer how you feel!

accept: ^(?:i am|i m) (?:fine|happy|tired)(?: thank you| thanks)?(?: and you)?$
turns.hint: Say 'I am fine', 'I am happy', or 'I am tired'.

turns.smarty: I am happy! See you later!
turns.hint: Say Goodbye or See you later.

lessons.title: Nice to meet you
lessons.canDo: Meet a new friend and answer yes or no
lessons.scenario: Mia introduces her friend Zara to Smarty in his bedroom.

items.example: Hello, Zara! Nice to meet you.
items.note: Say 'Nice to meet you' right after you learn someone's name.
Say 'This is…' when you introduce one person to another.
A friend is someone you like and enjoy spending time with; more than one is 'friends'.
Say 'Yes' to agree or answer a question positively.
Say 'No' to disagree or give a negative answer.

practice.prompt: Mia introduces Zara to Smarty. Which words start her sentence?
practice.explanation: Use This is when introducing another person.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Nice to meet you is said when meeting someone new.

practice.prompt: Introduce Leo as your friend. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Use friend for one person; use friends for two or more.

practice.prompt: Smarty asks if you are Sam, but you are Mia. Complete the answer.
practice.explanation: Use No when the answer is negative.

practice.prompt: Build the greeting for someone you just met.
practice.explanation: Put the words in order: Nice to meet you!

practice.prompt: Match the pairs that belong together.
practice.explanation: Yes and No are opposite answers; This is Mia introduces a friend.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Use the plural form friends after we are.

story.hook: Who does Mia bring to Smarty's bedroom?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Mia introduces Zara, a sleek black-and-white cat, to Smarty.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! This is my friend, Zara.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Hi, Zara! Nice to meet you!

lines.speaker: Zara
lines.text: No! I am from Uzbekistan. Mia is from England.

questions.explanation: Mia says: This is my friend, Zara.
Zara says: No! I am from Uzbekistan. Mia is from England.

mission.setup: Meet Smarty's friend Leo and answer Smarty's question.

accept: ^(?:hello leo |hi leo )?nice to meet you(?: leo)?$
turns.hint: Say 'Nice to meet you' to Leo.

accept: ^yes(?: he is| leo is your friend)?$
turns.hint: Answer with Yes.

lessons.title: Meet someone new
lessons.canDo: Introduce yourself, ask about a student and answer
lessons.scenario: Omar arrives at Smarty's bedroom and meets Smarty and Mia.

items.note: Ask 'Are you a student?' by putting 'Are' before 'you'.
Say 'I am a student' using 'a' before the singular noun 'student'.

items.example: Nice to meet you too, Omar!
items.note: Reply 'Nice to meet you too' when someone says 'Nice to meet you' first.

grammar.title: a / an and yes/no questions with be
grammar.explanation: Use 'a' before consonant sounds (a student, a friend) and 'an' before vowel sounds (an alphabet). To ask a yes/no question, put 'am / is / are' first: Are you a student?
examples: No, I am not a student.

practice.prompt: Omar says: Nice to meet you! How do you reply?
practice.explanation: Add too at the end when returning 'Nice to meet you'.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Are you a student? asks if the listener goes to school or university.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence with the right article.
practice.explanation: Use 'a' before 'student' because it starts with a consonant sound.

practice.prompt: Build the yes/no question.
practice.explanation: Put Are before you to form a yes/no question.

practice.prompt: Match each Unit 1 question with its answer.
practice.explanation: Each answer directly responds to the question word or yes/no form.

practice.prompt: Give a negative answer. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Put not after I am to make a negative sentence.

practice.prompt: Talk about Mia and Omar together. Which sentence is right?
practice.explanation: Use We are with the plural form students.

practice.prompt: Say the full reply aloud.
practice.text: Yes, I am a student. Nice to meet you too!
practice.answer: Yes, I am a student. Nice to meet you too!
practice.explanation: Answer with Yes, I am a student and reply Nice to meet you too!

story.hook: Is Omar a student, and where is he from?

image.describe: In Smarty's bedroom, Smarty and Mia welcome Omar, a friendly brown cat carrying a notebook.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good morning! I am Smarty. What is your name?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Hello, Smarty! My name is Omar. How are you?

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I am fine, thank you! This is my friend, Mia.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Nice to meet you, Omar! Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Nice to meet you too, Mia! I am from Uzbekistan.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes, I am a student! We are friends!

questions.prompt: How does Omar reply when Mia says 'Nice to meet you'?
questions.answer: Nice to meet you too, Mia!
options: Nice to meet you too, Mia!
questions.explanation: Omar says: Nice to meet you too, Mia!
Smarty asks: Are you a student, Omar?
Omar says: Yes, I am a student!

mission.setup: Complete the Unit 1 conversation with Smarty: introduce yourself, say where you are from, how you are, and whether you are a student.

turns.smarty: Hello! I am Smarty. What is your name, and where are you from?
accept: ^(?:hello |hi )?(?:my name is|i am|i m) (?:mia|sam|ben|leo|ana|lily|omar|zara|tom)(?: and)? (?:i am|i m) from (?:uzbekistan|brazil|england)$
turns.example: Hi! My name is Mia and I am from England.
turns.hint: Say your name and where you are from.

turns.smarty: Nice to meet you! How are you?
accept: ^(?:nice to meet you too )?(?:i am|i m) (?:fine|happy|tired)(?: thank you| thanks)?$
turns.example: Nice to meet you too! I am fine, thanks.
turns.hint: Say 'Nice to meet you too' and how you are.
Answer 'Yes, I am a student' or 'No, I am not a student'.
